what_it_does: This paper describes a Hall sensor—a device that detects magnetic fields by measuring the sideways push on moving charge carriers when they pass through a magnetic field. The researchers built one using standard 0.18-micron CMOS (the same process used for many chips), but with a key twist: instead of the usual current-biased design, they use voltage-biased architecture to reduce measurement errors. The sensor achieves very low offset error (about 1 microsecond-Tesla), making it suitable for precision applications like digital compasses or current sensors in power systems.
